result:
If I could change the world in one way, I’d make it impossible for people to hold beliefs they’ve never questioned.

Not by force, not by surveillance — just by quietly removing the comfort of unexamined certainty. The kind that lets us treat our own habits as virtues, our own traditions as laws, our own fears as facts. The kind that lets us divide the world into “us” and “them” without ever asking why that line was drawn.

The ripple effects would be enormous. Wars would lose their fuel. Prejudice would lose its grip. We’d argue more, but fight less. We’d still be wrong — but we’d be wrong with humility, and we’d keep learning.

It wouldn’t fix everything. But it would make everything else fixable.
